---
title: "Dtype Mapping"
subtitle: "Python-native types aligned"
format:
  typst:
    include-in-header: landscape.typ
---

+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| Python[^v]     | NumPy[^np]               | pandas[^pd]                | SQL / SQLite[^sq]            | GDAL / rasterio[^gdal]   |
+================+==========================+============================+==============================+==========================+
| `bool`         | `np.bool_`               | `bool` / `boolean`         | `BOOLEAN` (`INTEGER` 0/1)    | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `int`          | `np.int_`                | `int64` / `Int64`          | `INTEGER`                    | `Int16` … `UInt64`       |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `float`        | `np.float64`             | `float64`                  | `REAL` / `DOUBLE`            | `Float32` / `Float64`    |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `complex`      | `np.complex128`          | `complex128`               | –                            | `CFloat32` / `CFloat64`  |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `str`          | `'<U…'` / `np.str_`      | `str`                      | `TEXT`                       | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `bytes`        | `'|S…'` / `np.bytes_`    | `object`                   | `BLOB`                       | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `None`         | `object`                 | `NaN` / `pd.NA` / `NaT`    | `NULL`                       | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `datetime`     | `datetime64[us]`         | `datetime64[us]`           | `TIMESTAMP`                  | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `date`         | `datetime64[D]`          | `object`                   | `DATE`                       | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `timedelta`    | `timedelta64`            | `Timedelta`                | –                            | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `Decimal`      | `object`                 | `object`                   | `NUMERIC`                    | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+
| `dict`         | `object`                 | `object`                   | `TEXT` (JSON)                | –                        |
+----------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+------------------------------+--------------------------+

[^v]: Versions: NumPy 2.4.2, pandas 3.0.0, SQLite 3.51.2, GDAL 3.12.2, rasterio 1.5.0.
[^np]: No intrinsic nodata dtype; `NaN` only for floats; `object` dtype stores arbitrary Python objects (slow). `np.int_` is the platform default (usually `int64`).
[^pd]: Second form (`boolean`, `Int64`) is the nullable extension dtype. 3.0 default string dtype is `str` (pyarrow-backed if installed; missing is `NaN`). 3.0 infers datetime/timedelta units (often `[us]`). Dates stay `object`; convert with `pd.to_datetime`. Arrow decimal / JSON types are possible.
[^sq]: SQLite uses type affinity: `INTEGER` is signed 64-bit, `REAL` is an 8-byte float. Datetimes are stored as ISO 8601 `TEXT`, `REAL`, or Unix epoch `INTEGER`. No `INTERVAL` type.
[^gdal]: Raster band dtypes are numeric only; nodata/masks are metadata + mask band; "Byte" is `uint8`.
